note: Comping a ii–V–I in C with shell voicings: the shells drawn in a chord-shapes from the app's own shell shapes, then a strum-along with short chords on beats 2 and 4, then the root alone on 1 and 3 under them. Shows the chords counted the long way once, a pattern on every strum-along, and one extra line per block.

exercise.title: Comp the ii–V–I with shells
exercise.why: A shell is only the root, 3rd and 7th, so it is light enough to stop short, and short chords on beats 2 and 4 leave the gaps a melody needs.

cells.text: Dm7 is the 2nd chord in the key of C, G7 is the 5th and Cmaj7 is the 1st: in that order they make the ii–V–I. Below are their shell voicings, which leave out the 5th. Press a chord box below to hear one.

Press Play below to start the metronome. After a bar of count-in, the lit box shows the chord to play. Strum each shell on beats 2 and 4, and lift your fretting fingers a little to stop the sound short.
Practice until the next shell is under your fingers before its beat 2 comes.

Press Play below to start the metronome again. Pick the root, the lowest note of the shell, alone on beats 1 and 3, then strum the 3rd and 7th together on beats 2 and 4.
Practice until it is in your muscle memory: your picking hand finds the string of each root without you looking.
